text: The time taken by a boat to go 21 km downstream is equal to the time taken by it to go 9 km upstream. To go 12 km downstream and the same distance upstream, it takes a total of 5 5/7 hours. How much time (in hours) will the boat take to go 28 km downstream?

explanation.text:
Let the downstream speed be D and the upstream speed be U.

Equal times: 21/D = 9/U → D : U = 21 : 9 = 7 : 3. Take D = 7k and U = 3k.

Round trip of 12 km each way:
12/(7k) + 12/(3k) = 40/7
12/(7k) + 28/(7k) = 40/(7k) = 40/7 → k = 1

So D = 7 km/h and U = 3 km/h.

Time for 28 km downstream = 28 ÷ 7 = **4 hours** (option C).

text: The area of a rectangular field is 1008 m^2. Its shorter side is 1/8 of the sum of its longer side and one of its diagonals. What is the cost of fencing the field at ₹24 per m?

explanation.text:
Let the shorter side be b, the longer side l and the diagonal d.

Given b = (l + d)/8, so d = 8b − l.
Use d² = l² + b²:
(8b − l)² = l² + b²
64b² − 16bl + l² = l² + b²
63b² = 16bl → l = 63b/16

Area: l × b = 63b²/16 = 1008 → b² = 256 → b = 16 m, l = 63 m.
(Check: d = 8 × 16 − 63 = 65, and 63² + 16² = 4225 = 65² ✓)

Perimeter = 2(63 + 16) = 158 m
Cost = 158 × 24 = **₹3,792** (option C).

text:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct
order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
1) She was at the university working on her PhD thesis.
2) It was approaching 2 a.m. when Lexi made the discovery that would fracture the world.
3) The research involved creating controlled, miniature black holes in a Vacuity Machine and then
testing its potential for hyper-space travel which was mostly hypothetical research.
4) She skulled the rest of her black coffee and sat the paper cup down on the smooth, white table.

explanation.text:
- **2** is the opening: it sets the time ("approaching 2 a.m.") and introduces **Lexi** by name, together with the main event (the discovery).
- **4** follows with what she is doing at that moment (finishing her coffee); "She" refers back to Lexi.
- **1** gives background: she was at the university working on her **PhD thesis**.
- **3** explains what that research involved ("The research involved…"), which must come after the thesis is mentioned.
Order: **2-4-1-3**. Sentences 1 and 3 cannot open the paragraph because they use "She" and "The research" without anything introduced earlier.

answer.label: D

sectionRaw: Test of English Language and Comprehension
text:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct
order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
1) I carried a small load on my back as others knowing that it will help in getting to a new nation
that is about to be my nation and build a new life.
2) In the dead of the night, I walked with my family, away from my home, my street, my town, and
what was till yesterday - my country.
3) Even if they get on that train to Amritsar and arrive there in one piece, they would just be a wisp
of what they once were.
4) There were other families with us, snaking their way to Lahore railway station in fear, pain and
certainty that their lives are not theirs anymore.

explanation.text:
- **2** opens the scene: at night the narrator leaves home with family, leaving what was "till yesterday" their country.
- **4** widens the view: "There were **other families** with us", heading to Lahore railway station in fear and pain.
- **3** continues about those families: "Even if **they** get on that train to Amritsar…, they would just be a wisp of what they once were." "They" refers to the families in 4, so 3 must directly follow 4.
- **1** returns to the narrator, who carries a small load "as others" and hopes to build a new life in a new nation.
Order: **2-4-3-1**. Placing 1 between 4 and 3 would break the link between "other families" and "they".

answer.label: A

______, the suborbital tourist will travel in a rocket ______ the International Space Station only. Space
travel is not possible for everyone, ______ suborbital tourism is a possible alternative.

- Blank 1: parallel with present-tense "go": travellers go beyond… and **reach** the orbit of the moon. "reached" breaks the tense, so A is out.

The answer is **reach, hand, upto, but** (C).

No sooner did we arrived at the railway station than we got into an argument with the auto driver.

"No sooner … than" puts **inversion** after "No sooner": an auxiliary comes before the subject.

- Option B, "had we arrive", is wrong: *had* needs the past participle ("had we arrived").
Correct sentence: "No sooner **did we arrive** at the railway station than we got into an argument with the auto driver."

text: Identify the most suitable title for the given passage.
passage:
Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.
Good health is the soundness of body, mind and soul. It is that condition in which the body and
mind duly discharge their functions. Good health helps everyone to be creative and work for the
welfare of the society. He has to be, therefore, free from diseases: or, if he suffers from a disease
he needs treatments not only for that particular disease but for the whole body, mind and soul. In
other words, a doctor has to have a sound approach to the patients.
In these days of specialisation, doctors cure a patient only for his immediate disease, treating it in
isolation. Such an approach goes against the old aphorism that ‘prevention is better than cure’. Dr.
Hedge provides insight into the overall causes of simple and serious disease and describes the
methods of preventing them without having to take medicine but exercising, self-control on food
consumption, smoking and intake of alcoholic drinks. He also advocates regular yoga exercise and
meditation to keep fit, but at the same time warns against over indulgence.
Hedge stresses the importance of laughter because laughter induces secretion of good
catecholamine, which is a hormone produced by adrenal glands; they can be both beneficial and
harmful. They are harmful when a person is angry, but beneficial if he laughs. For a healthy living,
“Laughter proves to be great boon,” Hedge says.
In these days of hectic life, full of stress, strain and emotions, everyone needs to lead a relaxed life.
The best form of relaxation, according to Hedge, is sound sleep. “Restful sleep at night will
recharge our batteries for the following day’s fruitful endeavour,” he says. There is no use of lying
on the bed and tossing without sleep. Under those circumstances it is better to read or engage
oneself in some light mental activities which are useful. But never seek refuge in alcoholic drinks
or pills for inducing sleep, as these are not refreshing for an individual. For a normal human being,
eight hours of sleep a day is sufficient to keep him free from stress. More than nine to ten hours of
sleep a day would produce increased muscle protein loss in the body and might even shorten
one’s life.

explanation.text:
The underlined word is presumably **hectic**, as in "these days of **hectic** life, full of stress, strain…". *Hectic* means full of frantic, busy activity.
Its antonym is **leisurely**: unhurried, relaxed and done without haste.
- **Delayed** and **Postponed** mean put off to a later time. They are about timing, not the pace of life.

passage:
Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.
Good health is the soundness of body, mind and soul. It is that condition in which the body and
mind duly discharge their functions. Good health helps everyone to be creative and work for the
welfare of the society. He has to be, therefore, free from diseases: or, if he suffers from a disease
he needs treatments not only for that particular disease but for the whole body, mind and soul. In
other words, a doctor has to have a sound approach to the patients.
In these days of specialisation, doctors cure a patient only for his immediate disease, treating it in
isolation. Such an approach goes against the old aphorism that ‘prevention is better than cure’. Dr.
Hedge provides insight into the overall causes of simple and serious disease and describes the
methods of preventing them without having to take medicine but exercising, self-control on food
consumption, smoking and intake of alcoholic drinks. He also advocates regular yoga exercise and
meditation to keep fit, but at the same time warns against over indulgence.
Hedge stresses the importance of laughter because laughter induces secretion of good
catecholamine, which is a hormone produced by adrenal glands; they can be both beneficial and
harmful. They are harmful when a person is angry, but beneficial if he laughs. For a healthy living,
“Laughter proves to be great boon,” Hedge says.
In these days of hectic life, full of stress, strain and emotions, everyone needs to lead a relaxed life.
The best form of relaxation, according to Hedge, is sound sleep. “Restful sleep at night will
recharge our batteries for the following day’s fruitful endeavour,” he says. There is no use of lying
on the bed and tossing without sleep. Under those circumstances it is better to read or engage
oneself in some light mental activities which are useful. But never seek refuge in alcoholic drinks
or pills for inducing sleep, as these are not refreshing for an individual. For a normal human being,
eight hours of sleep a day is sufficient to keep him free from stress. More than nine to ten hours of
sleep a day would produce increased muscle protein loss in the body and might even shorten
one’s life.

The underlined word is presumably **creative**: "Good health helps everyone to be **creative**…". *Creative* means able to produce new and original ideas or things.

text: ‘अन्वेषण’ शब्द के शुद्ध सन्धि-विच्छेद का चयन कीजिये।
textHi: ‘अन्वेषण’ शब्द के शुद्ध सन्धि-विच्छेद का चयन कीजिये।

explanation.text:
'अन्वेषण' में **यण संधि** है।

नियम: यदि इ/ई, उ/ऊ, ऋ के बाद कोई भिन्न स्वर आए, तो इ/ई → य्, उ/ऊ → व्, ऋ → र् हो जाता है।

अनु + एषण: 'नु' का 'उ' और 'एषण' का 'ए' मिलते हैं। उ + ए → **व् + ए = वे**, इसलिए अनु + एषण = अन्वेषण। अतः उत्तर विकल्प B है।

अन्य विकल्प:
- अनु + वेषण: इससे 'अनुवेषण' बनेगा, अन्वेषण नहीं।
- अन्वे + षण: यह कृत्रिम विभाजन है; 'अन्वे' कोई सार्थक खंड नहीं।
- अना + एषण: आ + ए से वृद्धि संधि होकर 'ऐ' बनता, 'न्वे' नहीं।

इसी प्रकार के उदाहरण: अनु + अय = अन्वय, सु + आगत = स्वागत।

explanation.text:
'सदाचार' में **व्यंजन संधि** है: सत् + आचार = सदाचार।

नियम: वर्ग के पहले वर्ण (क्, च्, ट्, त्, प्) के बाद कोई स्वर या घोष वर्ण आए, तो पहला वर्ण अपने वर्ग का तीसरा वर्ण (ग्, ज्, ड्, द्, ब्) बन जाता है। यहाँ त् + आ → **दा**।

सन्धि-विच्छेद में मूल शब्द लिखे जाते हैं। मूल शब्द 'सत्' (अच्छा) और 'आचार' (आचरण) हैं, इसलिए सही उत्तर विकल्प A है।

अन्य विकल्प:
- सत् + अचार / सद् + अचार: 'अचार' के 'अ' से 'दा' (दीर्घ आ) नहीं बनता, और 'अचार' का अर्थ भी भिन्न है।
- सद् + आचार: 'सद्' संधि के बाद बना रूप है, मूल शब्द नहीं।

इसी प्रकार: सत् + आनंद = सदानंद, जगत् + ईश = जगदीश।

'मीनकेतु' में **बहुव्रीहि समास** है। इसमें दोनों पद मिलकर किसी तीसरे (अन्य) अर्थ की ओर संकेत करते हैं।

मीन = मछली, केतु = ध्वजा। 'मीन है केतु (ध्वजा) जिसकी, अर्थात कामदेव'। कामदेव की ध्वजा पर मछली का चिह्न माना जाता है।

बहुव्रीहि का विग्रह '…है जिसका/जिसकी, अर्थात/वह …' के रूप में किया जाता है। विकल्पों में केवल B इसी रूप में है, इसलिए वही उत्तर है। (मानक विग्रह 'मीन है केतु जिसकी' होगा; विकल्प का शब्द-क्रम थोड़ा शिथिल है।)

अन्य विकल्प:
- A: 'मीन वाला केतु' तत्पुरुष जैसा विग्रह है; यह अन्य अर्थ (कामदेव) नहीं बताता।
- C: अर्थ सही है, पर यह विग्रह के मानक रूप में नहीं है।
- D: केतु का अर्थ 'आँख' नहीं होता।

aiCheck.note: Option B is the only one in the standard बहुव्रीहि विग्रह form, though its wording ('मीन की केतु') is grammatically loose; the usual विग्रह is 'मीन है केतु (ध्वजा) जिसकी, अर्थात कामदेव'.

answer.label: B

concept: Hindi: लोकोक्ति एक दिन का पाहुना दूजे दिन अनखावना

explanation.text:
शुद्ध लोकोक्ति है **'एक दिन का पाहुना, दूजे दिन अनखावना'**।

- पाहुना = अतिथि/मेहमान
- अनखावना = अप्रिय लगने वाला, खटकने वाला

अर्थ: मेहमान एक दिन तो अच्छा लगता है, पर अधिक दिन ठहरने पर वह बोझ और अप्रिय लगने लगता है। अर्थात् अतिथि को अधिक दिन किसी के घर नहीं ठहरना चाहिए।

लोकोक्ति का दूसरा खंड 'दूजे दिन' कहता है, इसलिए पहले खंड में 'एक दिन' और 'पाहुना' (मेहमान) होना चाहिए। अतः उत्तर विकल्प C है।

'चार दिन का पाहुना' में 'एक दिन' और 'दूजे दिन' का क्रम टूट जाता है। 'आवना' और 'खावना' से अतिथि का भाव नहीं आता।

answer.label: C

explanation.text:
‘थकान’ का अर्थ है थक जाने की अवस्था (श्रम के बाद की शिथिलता)। इसके पर्यायवाची शब्द हैं: **क्लान्ति**, **श्रान्ति**, **परिश्रांति**, शिथिलता, थकावट।

**आश्विन** हिन्दू पंचांग का एक महीना (क्वार) है, जो भाद्रपद के बाद और कार्तिक से पहले आता है। इसका थकान से कोई संबंध नहीं है, इसलिए यह ‘थकान’ का पर्याय नहीं है।

अन्य विकल्प क्यों नहीं:
- क्लान्ति: थकावट, शिथिलता
- श्रान्ति: श्रम से उत्पन्न थकान
- परिश्रांति: अत्यधिक थकान

explanation.text:
विलोमार्थी-युग्म वह जोड़ा है जिसके दोनों शब्द एक-दूसरे के विपरीत अर्थ वाले हों।

- शुभ्र – श्वेत: दोनों का अर्थ ‘सफ़ेद’ है, यह पर्यायवाची युग्म है।
- व्याप्त – संकुचित: व्याप्त (फैला हुआ) का प्रचलित शुद्ध विलोम ‘अव्याप्त’ है; संकुचित का शुद्ध विलोम ‘विस्तृत/प्रसारित’ माना जाता है, अतः यह मानक युग्म नहीं है।
- शम्बर – पार्वती: इन दोनों शब्दों में विलोम संबंध नहीं है।

अतः उत्तर विकल्प 1 है।

तुरंत ही दूसरी आवश्यकता उपस्थित हो जाती है। उत्सव में हम किसी बात की आवश्यकता का अनुभव नहीं करते। यह आनंद जीवन का
आनंद है, काम का नहीं| उस दिन हम अपनी सारी आवश्यकताओं को भूल कर केवल मनुष्यत्व का ख्याल करते हैं। उस दिन हम अपनी

text:
What is the number of terms in the given expression?
(x^2 + 2/x)^11
concept: Number of terms in binomial expansion

explanation.text:
For a binomial raised to a power n, the expansion of (a + b)^n has **n + 1** terms, given by the general term T(r+1) = ⁿCᵣ · a^(n−r) · b^r for r = 0, 1, …, n.

Here a = x², b = 2/x and n = 11, so the number of terms is 11 + 1 = **12**.

The terms do not merge: the power of x in the general term is 2(11 − r) − r = 22 − 3r, which is different for every r from 0 to 11, so no two terms combine.

Why not the others:
- 11 is the exponent, not the number of terms.
- 22 and 24 come from doubling the exponent, which has no basis.

text: An unhappy employee because of ______ processes in a business can negatively affect the corporate image of the business and make the business less successful.

explanation.text:
Internal communication shapes how employees feel about the organisation. Unhappy employees serve customers badly and speak negatively about the firm, which damages the corporate image and reduces business success.

Why not the others:
- Frequent, instant and easy communication are positive qualities of a communication process; they would tend to make employees better informed and more satisfied, not unhappy.

Only 'poor communication' fits a cause of unhappiness, so option 1 is correct.

text: Haptic technology is used to provide ______ feedback to a user.

explanation.text:
**Haptic** comes from the Greek word for touch. Haptic technology recreates the sense of touch by applying forces, vibrations or motions to the user, i.e. it provides **tactile** (touch-based) feedback. Examples: a phone vibrating when a key is pressed, force-feedback game controllers and joysticks, and touch feedback in surgical simulators and VR gloves.

Why not the others:
- Olfactory relates to smell.
- Visual relates to sight (displays).
- Innovative is a general adjective, not a type of sensory feedback.

text: The process of organising the contents of each file into contiguous regions and creating larger areas of free space on the hard disk is called ______ and ______ is the process of making computer files take up less space on your computer by reducing the size of the file.

explanation.text:
Two disk/file utilities are described:

- **Defragmentation**: over time a file's pieces get scattered across non-adjacent clusters. A defragmenter rearranges each file into contiguous blocks and consolidates free space into larger areas, improving read speed on hard disks.
- **Compression**: reduces the size of a file (e.g. ZIP, RAR) so it takes less storage space and transfers faster.

So the blanks are defragmentation; compression.

Why not the others:
- Debugging removes program errors; assembly converts assembly code to machine code.
- Formatting prepares a disk for use and erases data.
- Mirroring (RAID 1) keeps duplicate copies of data on two disks; it increases, not reduces, space used.

ii) A compiler is a program which produces a machine level program from the specifications of a high-level language.

text: The given diagram expresses ______.
figureDescription: Four D flip-flops share a common clock; each D input comes from its own line of a common INPUTS bus and each Q goes to its own line of a common OUTPUTS bus, with no Q-to-D connection between flip-flops.

explanation.text:
Read the diagram's connections:
- **Inputs**: each of the four D flip-flops receives its D input directly from a separate input line, so all 4 bits are loaded simultaneously, i.e. parallel in.
- **Outputs**: each flip-flop's Q goes to a separate output line, so all 4 bits are available at the same time, i.e. parallel out.
- The flip-flops are not chained (no Q of one feeding D of the next), and all share one clock.

This is a **Parallel-In Parallel-Out (PIPO)** register: data is loaded and read in one clock pulse.

Why not the others:
- SIPO/SISO need a single serial input feeding the first flip-flop and Q→D chaining.
- PISO needs a single serial output from the last flip-flop.

text: Which of the following is a storage allocation scheme in which secondary memory can be addressed as though it were part of the main memory?

explanation.text:
**Virtual memory** is a storage allocation scheme in which secondary memory (disk) can be addressed as though it were part of main memory. Programs use virtual (logical) addresses; the OS and the MMU translate them to physical addresses, and pages not currently in RAM are kept on disk and brought in on demand (demand paging). This lets programs larger than physical RAM run and allows more processes in memory.

Why not the others:
- Secondary memory is the disk itself, not the scheme that maps it into the address space.
- CPU registers and buffers are small, fast storage inside or near the CPU and have nothing to do with addressing disk as main memory.

text: A ______ is the subset of a process and is also known as the lightweight process.

explanation.text:
A **thread** is the smallest unit of execution within a process. A process can contain several threads, which share the process's code, data, open files and address space, while each thread has its own program counter, registers and stack. Because creating and switching threads needs far less overhead than creating or switching processes, a thread is called a **lightweight process (LWP)**.

Why not the others:
- A program is passive code stored on disk.
- A library is a collection of reusable routines.
- A process is the heavyweight unit that contains threads, not a subset of itself.

text:
Which of the following statements is/are INCORRECT about the Z-buffer algorithm in computer graphics?
Statements:
i) It is an image space method to detect visible surface.
ii) In this method, a depth buffer is used to store the depth values of each position and a refresh (frame) buffer is used to store the intensity values or colour values for each position.
iii) In this method, object edges can be anti aliased.
iv) This method can only find one visible surface at each pixel position.

explanation.text:
Check each statement about the Z-buffer (depth-buffer) method:
- i) **Correct**. It works pixel by pixel in image space to decide which surface is visible.
- ii) **Correct**. It uses two buffers: a depth (Z) buffer holding the nearest depth for each pixel and a refresh/frame buffer holding the colour/intensity for each pixel.
- iii) **Incorrect**. Because it keeps only one depth and one colour per pixel, it cannot blend partial coverage at edges, so object edges cannot be anti-aliased (the A-buffer method was developed to fix this).
- iv) **Correct**. Storing a single depth per pixel means it finds only one visible surface per pixel, which is why it cannot handle transparency directly.

Only iii is incorrect, so the answer is option 4.

text:
Which of the given options best describes the truthfulness of the following statements?
i) In the probability theory, an outcome is the result of a random experiment.
ii) The purpose of statistical inference is to estimate the uncertainty or sample to sample variation.
iii) A sampling error is the difference between the true population values (called parameters) and the measured sample values (called statistics).

explanation.text:
- i) **True**. In probability theory, an outcome is a possible result of a random experiment (e.g. getting 'Heads' when tossing a coin); the set of all outcomes is the sample space.
- ii) **True**. Statistical inference draws conclusions about a population from a sample. Since different samples give different results, a central purpose is to estimate this uncertainty, i.e. sample-to-sample variation, through standard errors, confidence intervals and hypothesis tests.
- iii) **True**. Sampling error is the difference between a population value (parameter, e.g. μ) and the corresponding value measured from a sample (statistic, e.g. x̄), arising because only part of the population is observed.

All three are true, so option 1 is correct.

text:
Which of the following is/are associated with turbulent flow?
i) Flow of liquid is orderly.
ii) Flow of liquid is zigzag and random.

explanation.text:
In fluid flow there are two main regimes:
- **Streamline (laminar) flow**: the liquid moves in smooth, parallel layers; the velocity at a point stays constant, so the flow is orderly. This happens at low speeds (low Reynolds number).
- **Turbulent flow**: above a critical velocity (high Reynolds number) the motion becomes irregular, with eddies and whirls; particles move in a **zigzag, random** manner.

Statement i (orderly flow) describes laminar/streamline flow, not turbulent flow. Statement ii describes turbulent flow.

So only (ii) is associated with turbulent flow: option 2.

The output (Q or Q′) of each flip-flop drives the clock input of the next one, so a change 'ripples' through the chain one stage after another. This makes it simple but slower, since the propagation delays add up.

Why not the others:
- Synchronous counter: all flip-flops share the same clock and change state together.
- Ring counter: a shift register whose last output is fed back to the first input, with a common clock.
- 'Cascaded' only describes connecting stages in series; it is not the name of this counter type.

text:
Consider the following disk request sequence for a disk with 100 tracks:
60, 45, 21, 67
Head pointer starting at 60 and moving in the left direction. Find the number of head movements in cylinders using FCFS scheduling.

explanation.text:
FCFS (First Come First Served) services requests strictly in arrival order; the direction ('moving left') does not matter for FCFS.

Head starts at 60. Requests: 60, 45, 21, 67.
- 60 → 60: |60 − 60| = 0
- 60 → 45: |60 − 45| = 15
- 45 → 21: |45 − 21| = 24
- 21 → 67: |67 − 21| = 46

Total head movement = 0 + 15 + 24 + 46 = **85 cylinders**.

So option 1 is correct. The direction information would matter only for algorithms like SCAN, C-SCAN or LOOK.

text: In Managed Ad-hoc Network (MANET), under which attack, malicious node injects fault routing information to the network, in order to locate packets into a loop?

explanation.text:
In a MANET (Mobile Ad-hoc Network) every node also acts as a router, so a compromised node can disrupt routing.

In a **Byzantine attack**, a compromised intermediate node (or a set of colluding nodes) injects false routing information and creates **routing loops**, forwards packets along non-optimal paths, or selectively drops packets. This disrupts or degrades routing services while being hard to detect.

Why not the others:
- Wormhole attack: two colluding nodes tunnel packets between distant points through a private link, misleading others about route lengths.
- Snooping: eavesdropping on traffic to read data, not altering routes.
- DNS attack: targets name resolution (e.g. DNS spoofing), not ad-hoc routing loops.

So option 1 is correct.

text:
What is the degree of the following function?
F(A,B,C,D) = A′B′C′D′

explanation.text:
In Boolean algebra, the **degree** of a product term (minterm) is the number of literals in it, i.e. the number of variables that appear (complemented or not).

F(A,B,C,D) = A′B′C′D′ contains four literals: A′, B′, C′ and D′. So its degree is **4**. It is a minterm (m₀) of the four-variable function, the only input combination that makes F = 1 being A = B = C = D = 0.

Why not the others:
- 8 has no basis here (it is just 2 × 4).
- 0 would mean a constant.
- 5 exceeds the number of variables.

So option 1 is correct.

text: Which of the following security services protects against repudiation?

explanation.text:
**Repudiation** means a sender or receiver later denies having sent or received a message. - **Authentication** confirms the identity of a communicating party.
- **Data integrity** ensures the data was not modified in transit.

text:
Find the rank of the given matrix.
[ 1 5 6 ]
[ 2 3 4 ]
[ −1 2 2 ]
figureDescription: A 3×3 matrix with rows (1, 5, 6), (2, 3, 4) and (−1, 2, 2).

explanation.text:
Matrix rows: (1, 5, 6), (2, 3, 4), (−1, 2, 2).
**Step 1: determinant.**
det = 1(3·2 − 4·2) − 5(2·2 − 4·(−1)) + 6(2·2 − 3·(−1))
= 1(6 − 8) − 5(4 + 4) + 6(4 + 3)
= −2 − 40 + 42 = 0
So the rank is less than 3.
**Step 2: find a non-zero 2×2 minor.** From the first two rows and columns: 1·3 − 5·2 = −7 ≠ 0.
So the rank is **2** (option A). (Check: R₃ = R₂ − R₁ gives (2−1, 3−5, 4−6) = (1, −2, −2) = −(−1, 2, 2), so the rows are dependent.)
Why not the others: a 3×3 matrix can never have rank greater than 3, so 6, 9 and 4 are impossible.

text:
Which of the given options best describes the truthfulness of the following statements?
i) A compiler translates the entire source code line by line.
ii) Computer architecture refers to those attributes of a system visible to a programmer.
iii) The Reduced Instruction Set Architecture (RISC) computer organisation reduces the cycles per instruction at the cost of the number of instructions per program to increase the CPU performance.
iv) All the arithmetic and logical processing is performed by the Arithmetic Logic Unit under the supervision of a control unit.
concept: Compiler vs interpreter; architecture vs organisation; RISC

explanation.text:
Check each statement:
- i) **False**. A compiler translates the **entire program at once** into object code; translating line by line is what an **interpreter** does.
- ii) **True**. Computer architecture is the set of attributes visible to the programmer (instruction set, data types, addressing modes, I/O mechanisms); organisation is how they are implemented.
- iii) **True**. CPU time = instructions/program × cycles/instruction × time/cycle. RISC lowers cycles per instruction (simple, often single-cycle instructions) but needs more instructions per program.
- iv) **True**. The ALU performs arithmetic and logical operations, while the control unit directs and supervises it.
So i-False, ii-True, iii-True, iv-True: option B.

answer.label: B

text:
A stack is a liner data structure in which insertion and deletion of elements are done at only one end, which is known as the top of the stack. Stack is called a last-in, first-out (LIFO) structure because the last element which is added to the stack is the first element which is deleted from the stack.
Top → L
M
N
O
P
Bottom → Q
Read the above paragraph and answer the following.
Which of the following items will be at the top in the stack after removing three items?
figureDescription: A vertical stack of six boxes labelled, from Top to Bottom: L, M, N, O, P, Q.

explanation.text:
In a stack, removal (pop) always happens at the **top**, following LIFO.
Stack from top to bottom: L, M, N, O, P, Q.
- Pop 1 removes **L** → top is M
- Pop 2 removes **M** → top is N
- Pop 3 removes **N** → top is **O**
After three removals the stack is O, P, Q with **O** on top, which is option A.
Why not the others: L is the original top (no removal); N is the third item removed, so it is no longer in the stack; P would be on top only after four removals.

answer.label: A

text: Which of the following devices works at the network layer of the ISO-OSI reference model?

explanation.text:
A **router** works at the **network layer (Layer 3)**. It reads the logical (IP) address in each packet and forwards it between different networks using its routing table.
Why not the others:
- **Hub**: Layer 1 (physical); it repeats incoming signals out of all ports.
- **Repeater**: Layer 1; it regenerates a signal to extend cable length.
- **Amplifier**: boosts an analog signal, also at the physical level.
(For reference: switches and bridges work at Layer 2, data link; gateways can work up to Layer 7.) So the answer is option B.

text:
Which of the given options best describes the truthfulness of the following statements?
i) The clock signal is required for sequential circuits.
ii) In the sequential circuit, memory elements play an important role and are required.
concept: Sequential circuits: clock and memory elements

explanation.text:
- ii) **True**. A sequential circuit's output depends on present inputs **and past state**, so it must contain memory elements (flip-flops or latches, or feedback loops). This is what separates it from a combinational circuit.
- i) **Depends on the type.** Sequential circuits are of two kinds:
- **Synchronous**: state changes only on clock pulses, so a clock is required.
- **Asynchronous**: state changes as soon as inputs change; no clock is used.
Many comparison tables simply say 'combinational: no clock; sequential: clock required', and the source key (option A, both true) follows that view. Strictly, because asynchronous sequential circuits exist, statement i is not true for all sequential circuits, which gives i-False, ii-True (option B). The question is therefore ambiguous. In an exam, A is the answer the setter intended.

aiCheck.note: Statement i is true only for synchronous sequential circuits; asynchronous sequential circuits have no clock. The key (A) follows the common combinational-vs-sequential comparison table that lists the clock as 'required'. Strictly, i is false (option B).

text:
Which of the following statements is/are true for the Waterfall Model?
Statements:
i) This model does not work smoothly if there are some issues left at the previous step.
ii) It projects the process of development in a cyclic manner, repeating every step after every cycle of software development life cycle process.
iii) This model considers risk, which often goes unnoticed by most other models.
iv) This model provides means of testing of software at each stage in a reverse manner.
concept: Waterfall model characteristics vs Spiral and V-model

explanation.text:
Check each statement:
- i) **True**. Waterfall is linear and sequential: each phase starts only after the previous one is finished, and going back is costly. Issues left unresolved in an earlier phase disrupt everything that follows.
- ii) **False**. Developing in repeated cycles describes the **Spiral** or **iterative** models, not Waterfall.
- iii) **False**. Explicit risk analysis in every cycle is the hallmark of the **Spiral** model; Waterfall has no risk-handling phase.
- iv) **False**. A testing phase for each development stage, drawn in a V shape, describes the **V-model** (verification and validation model).
So only statement i is true: option A.

text:
What is/are the purpose(s) of JavaScript events?
i) Provide a dynamic interface to a webpage.
ii) Provide a static interface to a webpage.

explanation.text:
**JavaScript events** are actions or occurrences in the browser, such as `click`, `mouseover`, `keydown`, `load`, `submit` and `change`. Event handlers attached to them (e.g. `onclick`, or `addEventListener`) run code in response, so the page can react to the user: show or hide content, validate forms, update text, play animations and so on. Their purpose is to give a webpage a **dynamic, interactive interface**.
A static interface is what plain HTML and CSS already provide without any event handling; events exist precisely to go beyond that.
So only statement (i) is correct: option A.

text: ______ is a method of constructing new data points within a range of discrete set of known data points.

explanation.text:
**Interpolation** estimates new values that lie **within the range** of a discrete set of known data points. For example, if f(1) = 2 and f(3) = 6, linear interpolation gives f(2) ≈ 4. Common methods are linear, Lagrange, Newton's forward/backward difference and spline interpolation.
Estimating values **outside** the known range is called **extrapolation**.
Why not the others:
- **Integration** finds the area under a curve (accumulation).
- **Limit** is the value a function approaches as its input approaches some point.
- **Isolation** is not a method for constructing data points.
So the answer is option A.

text: Which of the following is NOT a system call category?

explanation.text:
System calls are the interface through which programs request OS services. The standard categories (Silberschatz) are:
- **Process control**: fork/create, exit, wait, load, execute.
- **File manipulation (management)**: create, open, read, write, close, delete.
- **Device manipulation (management)**: request, release, read and write devices.
- **Information maintenance**: get or set time, date and system data.
- **Communication**: create connections, send and receive messages, shared memory.
- **Protection**: get or set permissions.
**Data compilation** is not a system call category. Compiling is done by a user-level program (the compiler), not by the OS kernel. So the answer is option D.

text:
Which of the given options best describes the truthfulness of the following statements?
i) In connectionless services of transport layer protocol, the packets are sent from one party to another with no need for connection establishment or connection release.
ii) In connection-oriented service of transport layer protocol, a connection is first established between the sender and the receiver.
iii) The User Datagram Protocol (UDP) is called a connectionless, unreliable transport protocol.

explanation.text:
Check each statement:
- i) **True**. In a connectionless service (e.g. UDP), each packet is sent independently; there is no connection setup or teardown phase.
- ii) **True**. In a connection-oriented service (e.g. TCP), a connection is first established (TCP's three-way handshake), then data is transferred, and finally the connection is released.
- iii) **True**. UDP is described as a **connectionless, unreliable** transport protocol: no handshake, no acknowledgements, no retransmission and no flow control. Its only error check is an optional checksum.
All three are true: option A.

text: ______ is a study of economics based on facts, is verifiable, and you can prove or disprove it.

explanation.text:
**Positive economics** describes and explains economic phenomena **as they are**. Its statements are factual and can be tested against data, i.e. verified or disproved. Example: 'An increase in the minimum wage reduces employment among teenagers' can be checked with evidence.
Its counterpart is **normative economics**, which deals with what **ought to be**. It involves value judgements that cannot be proved, e.g. 'The government should raise the minimum wage.'
'Negative', 'regular' and 'basic' economics are not standard branches here; the usual contrast is positive vs normative. So the answer is option A.

text: When a plane is perpendicular to a reference plane, its projection on that plane is a/an ______.
concept: Projection of a plane perpendicular to the projection plane

explanation.text:
In orthographic projection, the projectors are perpendicular to the reference (projection) plane. When a flat surface (plane figure) is **perpendicular** to that reference plane, the observer looks at it edge-on, so all its points project onto a single **straight line** (its edge view).
For comparison:
- A plane **parallel** to the reference plane projects in its true shape and size.
- A plane **inclined** to it projects as a smaller, distorted shape.
- A **line** perpendicular to a reference plane projects as a **point**, which is the trap in option A.
So the answer is option B.

answer.label: B

text: Which of the following does the actual display in a computer?

explanation.text:
The device that **actually displays** the image is the monitor. Among the options, that is the **CRT** (cathode ray tube): an electron beam strikes the phosphor-coated screen to produce visible pixels.
Why not the others:
- **VRAM** (video RAM) is the memory that holds the frame buffer (the image to be shown), but it does not display anything itself.
- **GPU** computes and renders the image into the frame buffer.
- **DPU** (display processing unit) prepares or processes the display data.
Each of these produces or stores the picture; the CRT is what shows it. So the answer is option A.

Knowledge-management literature commonly separates three types:

This gives a-ii, b-iii, c-i: option A.

Which of the given options best describes the truthfulness of the following statements?
i) A tuple is a sequence of immutable Python objects, in the given tuple course = "l", "m", "n", "o", has four elements.
ii) To explicitly remove an entire tuple, use the drop statement.
concept: Python tuples: packing and deletion with del

explanation.text:
- i) **True**. A tuple is an ordered, **immutable** sequence. Writing `course = "l", "m", "n", "o"` (without brackets) still creates a tuple by **tuple packing**: `('l', 'm', 'n', 'o')`, and `len(course)` is 4.
- ii) **False**. Python has no `drop` statement. Since a tuple is immutable you cannot delete individual elements, but you can remove the whole tuple with the **`del`** statement: `del course`. Using `course` afterwards raises a `NameError`. (`DROP` is an SQL command for removing tables.)
So i-True, ii-False: option C.

i) Interpolation is a statistical method by which related known values are used to estimate an unknown value or set of values.
ii) In the Inverse Distance Weighted (IDW) interpolation method, estimation of cell values is done by averaging values of sample data points in the neighbourhood of each processing cell.

This matches the standard description, e.g. in ArcGIS documentation: cell values are found by averaging the values of sample points near each processing cell.
Both are true: option A.

text:
Which of the following is/are Interpolation Methods in Computer Graphics?
i) Inverse Distance Weighted
ii) Kriging
iii) Natural Neighbor
iv) Spline
v) Topo to raster
vi) Compiler

options.label: A
options.text: i, ii, iii, iv and v only

options.label: B
options.text: i, ii, iii, iv, v and vi

explanation.text:
These are the surface interpolation methods used to build raster surfaces from sample points (they come from GIS tools such as ArcGIS Spatial Analyst, although the question calls them computer graphics):
- **Inverse Distance Weighted (IDW)**: weighted average with weights that fall off with distance.
- **Kriging**: geostatistical method based on spatial autocorrelation (semivariogram).
- **Natural Neighbor**: uses Voronoi (Thiessen) polygon areas as weights.
- **Spline**: fits a smooth, minimum-curvature surface through the points.
- **Topo to Raster**: builds hydrologically correct elevation models from contours and points.
A **compiler** translates source code into machine code and has nothing to do with interpolation.
So i to v are interpolation methods: option A.

answer.label: A

text: Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan was launched in _______ year.
textHi: सर्व शिक्षा अभियान _______ वर्ष में लोकार्पित किया गया था।

explanation.text:
**Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA)** was launched by the Government of India in **2001** (programme year 2000-01) under Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee. Its aim was **universal elementary education** for all children aged 6-14 years, in a time-bound way.
The goal gained legal force with the **86th Constitutional Amendment (2002)**, which added Article 21A, and the **RTE Act, 2009**. In 2018, SSA was merged with RMSA and Teacher Education into the integrated **Samagra Shiksha** scheme.

text:
Which of the following is an element of effective learning activity?
I. Spontaneous involvement
II. Challenging
textHi:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा प्रभावी अधिगम क्रियाकलाप का एक तत्व है?
I. स्वतः भागीदारी
II. चुनौतीपूर्णता

options.label: D
options.textHi: ना ही I ना ही II

explanation.text:
An effective learning activity usually has both features.
- **Spontaneous involvement**: the activity is interesting and meaningful, so children take part willingly and actively, without being forced. This makes learning joyful and participatory.
- **Challenging**: the task is pitched slightly beyond what the child can already do (in Vygotsky's terms, within the zone of proximal development). It makes children think, explore and solve problems without being so hard that they give up.
So the answer is **Both I and II**.

text:
The Rishi valley approach in pedagogy was designed to make the students______.
I. capable of acquiring mastery in learning competencies through both group and individual
learning
II. Understand the importance of physical environment in the classroom
textHi:
शिक्षाशास्त्र में ऋषि घाटी उपागम को छात्रों को ______ डिज़ाइन किया गया था।
I. समूह और व्यक्तिगत अधिगम दोनों के माध्यम से अधिगम दक्षताओ में महारत हासिल करने में सक्षम बनाने के लिए
II. कक्षा में भौतिक वातावरण के महत्व को समझने के लिए

options.label: D
options.textHi: ना ही I ना ही II

explanation.text:
The **Rishi Valley approach** (the RIVER model from the Rishi Valley Institute for Educational Resources, Andhra Pradesh) was designed for **multigrade, multilevel** rural classrooms. Learning is organised as a **"learning ladder"** of small milestones with activity cards, so each child moves at their own pace. Children work through **individual, small-group and whole-class** activities until they gain **mastery of the learning competencies**. This matches statement **I**.
The approach uses an organised, child-friendly classroom, but teaching the importance of the physical environment is not its stated aim, so statement II is not its purpose. The answer is **Only I**.

text:
The objective type items are normally used in most of the tests. Which of the following is the
correct example of closed-ended items?
textHi:
अधिकांश परीक्षणों में वस्तुनिष्ठ प्रकार के पद का सामान्य रूप से उपयोग किया जाता है। निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा बंद-पद का सही
उदाहरण है?

options.label: A
options.text: In how many ways can you draw a triangle?
options.textHi: आप कितने तरीकों से एक त्रिभुज बना सकते हैं?

options.label: B
options.textHi: कौन-सी संख्याएँ जोड़ने पर 7 प्रदान करती हैं?

options.label: C
options.text: Write down as many words adding ‘ed’ like played, created etc.
options.textHi: ' ed ' जोड़ते हुए जितने शब्द लिख सकते है लिखे, जैसे played, created आदि।

options.label: D
options.text: Who controls the teachers and students in a school?
options.textHi: एक विद्यालयमें शिक्षकों और छात्रों को कौन नियंत्रित करता है?

explanation.text:
A **closed-ended** item has **one fixed, correct answer**. An **open-ended** item allows many acceptable answers and divergent thinking.
- **A**: "In how many ways can you draw a triangle?" Many approaches; open-ended.
- **B**: "Which numbers when added give 7?" Many pairs (3+4, 5+2, 6+1…); open-ended.
- **C**: "Write as many words adding 'ed'…" Many possible answers; open-ended.
- **D**: "Who controls the teachers and students in a school?" One expected answer (the **principal**/head of the school); **closed-ended**.
So D is the closed-ended item.

answer.label: D

text:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding formative assessment?
I. It is conducted at regular intervals on informal basis.
II. It involves self-assessment and peer appraisal.
III. It is diagnostic and remedial.
textHi:
सृजनात्मक आंकलन के सन्दर्भ में निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन सही है?
I. यह अनौपचारिक आधार पर नियमित अंतराल से आयोजित किया जाता है।
II. इसमें स्व-आंकलन और समकक्ष मूल्यांकन शामिल है।
III. यह निदानात्मक और उपचारात्मक है।

explanation.text:
All three statements describe **formative assessment**, which takes place during teaching to improve learning.
- **I**: it is ongoing, **conducted at regular intervals**, often informally (observation, oral questions, class work, quizzes).
- **II**: it encourages **self-assessment and peer assessment**, so learners take part in judging and improving their own work.
- **III**: it is **diagnostic and remedial**: it identifies learning gaps and leads to corrective teaching.
The answer is **I, II and III**.

matches.reason: Both test features of formative assessment (regular, informal, diagnostic, remedial).

text:
What is regional art?
I. It is the work of a community of unschooled artists keeping alive the traditions specific to its
particular culture.
II. It reflects the traditional art forms of diverse community groups.
textHi:
क्षेत्रीय कला क्या है?
I. यह विशिष्ट परंपराओं को उनकी विशेष संस्कृति के लिए जीवित रखने के लिए अशिक्षित कलाकारों के समुदाय का काम है।
II. यह विविध सामुदायिक समूहों के पारंपरिक कला रूपों को दर्शाती है।

options.label: D
options.textHi: ना ही I ना ही II

explanation.text:
**Regional art** (folk art) is the traditional art of a particular region or community.
- **I**: it is produced by communities of **unschooled** (not formally trained) artists who keep alive the **traditions** of their own culture. Skills pass from generation to generation, for example Madhubani, Warli and Gond painting.
- **II**: it reflects the **traditional art forms of diverse community groups**, so each region and community has its own styles, motifs and materials.
Both statements describe regional art, so the answer is **Both I and II**.

text:
The initial Juvenile Justice act, 1986, defined a boy child below ________ of age and a girl child as
below _______ of age, a juvenile.
textHi:
प्रारंभिक किशोर न्याय अधिनियम, 1986 ने ________ से कम आयु के लड़के और _______ से कम आयु की लड़की को किशोर के रूप
में परिभाषित किया है।

explanation.text:
The **Juvenile Justice Act, 1986** defined a **juvenile** as a **boy below 16 years** of age or a **girl below 18 years** of age.
This difference by sex was removed by the **Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000**, which set a uniform age of **18 years** for both boys and girls, in line with the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child. The **2015 Act** kept 18 years but allows children aged 16-18 accused of heinous offences to be tried as adults after assessment.
So the blanks are filled by **16 years, 18 years**.

text:
‘Problem related to languages’ is one of the hurdles to school-family-community partnerships.
Which of the following actions can be taken with respect to this hurdle?
I. Set aside a room in the school in which to provide child care during events.
II. Have printed materials translated into home languages.
III. Help parents set up car pools.
textHi:
भाषाओं से संबंधित समस्या' विद्यालय-परिवार-समुदाय की साझेदारी में एक बाधा है। इस बाधा के सन्दर्भ में निम्नलिखित में से कौन सी
कार्रवाई की जा सकती है?
I. विद्यालय में एक कमरा अलग रखें जिसमें आयोजनों के दौरान बच्चों की देखभाल प्रदान की जाए।
II. मुद्रित सामग्री का घरेलू भाषाओं में अनुवाद करवाना।
III. कार पूल स्थापित करने में माता-पिता की सहायता करें।

explanation.text:
The hurdle here is **language**: some parents may not understand the language the school uses, so they cannot follow notices or take part in school activities.
- **II. Translating printed materials** (notices, newsletters, report cards) into the families' **home languages** directly removes this barrier.
- **I. Child care during events** addresses a different hurdle: parents who cannot attend because of young children at home.
- **III. Helping set up car pools** addresses **transportation** problems.
Only II deals with the language problem, so the answer is **Only II**.
